page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-24-lssd belongs to the Network Optimized family, engineered for high-throughput, memory-demanding infrastructure. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture paired with 186.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server does not incorporate GPU acceleration, dedicating its host resources entirely to CPU compute, high memory density, and local I/O handling.

The storage subsystem includes 1611 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 4 drives. This local NVMe implementation provides low-latency, high-IOPS storage directly on the hypervisor host, removing network transit overhead for disk operations. In terms of public networking, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on private VPC topologies, Cloud NAT, or associated external network routing for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high-density combination of substantial memory and integrated local NVMe disks eliminates the need for expensive high-tier networked block storage in performance-sensitive scenarios. However, because local NVMe storage is ephemeral by nature, workloads must account for data persistence through external replication or snapshots. This hardware configuration fits in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-performance search clusters.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-24-lssd is an x86_64 instance from the Network Optimized family configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 186.0 GB of memory. Designed for resource-intensive applications, it delivers a memory-dense ratio of 7.75 GB per core without discrete GPU acceleration. The instance incorporates 1611 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across 4 drives, offering high-throughput, low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host. System networking requires dedicated routing or VPC configuration as complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the coupled memory and integrated NVMe hardware, which reduces reliance on external network storage for high-IOPS tasks. Given its memory capacity and fast ephemeral storage, this configuration is well aligned with workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed data caches, real-time analytics engines, and transactional database clusters requiring substantial caching capacity.
